comments.author: @i2c_jason
comments.text: My company is working on something a little bit similar for prompting 3D parametric models (the real deal 3D for engineering). The main idea being that we don't need engineers (such as myself) to ingest all of the product design requirements, ideate a 3D model, and create all of the related project outputs. This can be done by an agentic workflow with model-agnostic API calls and some good ol fashioned expert system calls. Multiply all of that by spawned Jupyter notebooks in an iterative ideation loop, add a minimalist web UI for tweaking latent spaces with some human oversight, and there's a recipe for some serious heavy lifting within mechanical and electrical engineering disciplines. I just hope we can deploy this thing before twenty others do. Either way, the learning will be super valuable to our startup (BerylCNC) and it will be a foundation for scalable growth in this space.

comments.author: @Urgelt
comments.text:
Seems to me that this AI Researcher idea will break science.

$15 for a credible paper? At that cost, we can't publish more than a tiny fraction of AI- generated papers in peer-reviewed journals. Humans won't be able to read them all. Or even very many.

So peer review will move to AI, too - different models critiquing AI-generated papers and endorsing or rejecting them. And publication? Sharing between AI models, mostly.

Thing is, it takes capital to move from basic research to product development. We are a long, long way from trusting AI with capital allocation decisions. So we get papers only AI can read, with little connection to product development.

I'm sure there are ways through that thicket. But science will be changed beyond recognition.

There are of course garbage in, garbage out pitfalls.
Example: The James Web Space Telescope discovered  mature spiral galaxies in the 'Dark Ages'. This was supposed to be an epoch right after a supposed Big Bang , but instead of a Dark Ages, the James Webb Space Telescope sees this volume smack full of garden variety spiral galaxies, rather than a volume void of anything other than disassociated particles.
The Dark Ages is a logical extension of interpreting cosmic redshift as an evolutionary tool, but it was wrong, because we now know there is no Dark Ages. Since the Dark Ages does not exist, then the cosmic redshift interpretation is wrong. 
Yet cosmologists still insist on using cosmic redshift as an evolutionary measuring tool, churning out papers as if this this plain observational evidence was not a heads-up moment, a paradigm questioning the very existence of a 'Big Bang'
Consequently, the research AI would be absorbing all these erroneous papers, forcing it to continuously hallucinate. 
Perhaps it would have better luck in other, more scientific disciplines.
